title: Let a tenant clear a setting in a concurrent map

blocks.text: Tenant settings are read by every request thread and changed from the admin page, so they live in a `ConcurrentHashMap`. Tenants can now **clear** a setting, and that is not the same as never setting it: a tenant who clears the invoice footer wants no footer, while a tenant who never set one gets the platform's default footer.

items: `encode(value)`: what to store for a value the tenant set, `null` included;
`decode(stored)`: the tenant's value back from what `encode` stored;
`isSet(name)`: whether the tenant ever set the setting, cleared or not.

blocks.text: Any text a tenant types must read back exactly as typed, whatever it is. About five lines in total. The tests use one thread.

cases.says: a value the tenant set reads back as itself and is the effective value
a setting the tenant never set reads as null and falls back to the platform default
a setting the tenant cleared reads as null
an empty value is a value: it reads back as empty, not as cleared
any text a tenant types, the word null included, reads back as itself and is never taken for a cleared setting
a cleared setting counts as set, so it overrides the platform default with nothing

origin.section: ConcurrentHashMap Refuses null, So That null from get Means Absent

concepts: A stand-in for null in a map that refuses null must be a value no caller can store; an empty string collides with a real empty value.
